title: Turn finished jobs into proof, repeat work and a 90-day plan
course_title: Freelancing Fundamentals: Package, Price and Deliver Paid Work

say: Turn finished jobs into proof, repeat work, and a 90-day plan.
This is the video for module four of Freelancing Fundamentals.
Your first clients are hard to win because strangers have no proof that you are good.

panel.heading: Every job is a chance to build proof
items: Strangers have no proof you are good
Repeat clients cost less time to win

say: Every finished job is a chance to create that proof. Ask for feedback, collect a testimonial, and record what you achieved.

panel.heading: Every job is a chance to build proof
items: Strangers have no proof you are good
Repeat clients cost less time to win

say: Then offer the next piece of work, because repeat clients take far less time to win.

panel.heading: Every job is a chance to build proof
items: Strangers have no proof you are good
Repeat clients cost less time to win

say: Finally, you will build a realistic plan for your next 90 days.

say: Ask while the client is still pleased. For example, Ifeoma finished a month of captions for Ada's Cakes and messaged four days later.

panel.heading: Collect a strong testimonial
items: Ask within a few days of handover
Type up her words and ask permission

say: General questions get answers like good job, thanks. So ask: what was the main problem before, what has changed since, and what could I do better?

panel.heading: Collect a strong testimonial
items: Ask within a few days of handover
Type up her words and ask permission

say: Ada replied with a voice note. Ifeoma typed up the key sentences and asked: may I use these words, with your name and business, on my page? Ada agreed.

panel.heading: Collect a strong testimonial
items: Ask within a few days of handover
Type up her words and ask permission

say: Then Ifeoma wrote a case snapshot in three lines. Problem: posts had no prices. Work: 12 captions with price, size and order steps. Result: customers now ask fewer questions before ordering.

panel.heading: Collect a strong testimonial
items: Ask within a few days of handover
Type up her words and ask permission

say: Use the client's own words for the result. Never invent numbers like sales doubled, and never put a client's name on words you wrote yourself.

panel.heading: Collect a strong testimonial
items: Ask within a few days of handover
Type up her words and ask permission
panel.rule: Never write a testimonial yourself or invent results

say: Keep all your proof in one Google Drive folder, so you can send the right item in seconds.

panel.heading: Referrals and the next job
items: Keep proof in one Drive folder
Show your best two or three pieces
Offer a concrete next piece of work

say: Show your best two or three pieces where clients look: your WhatsApp Business catalogue, LinkedIn, or your platform profile.

panel.heading: Referrals and the next job
items: Keep proof in one Drive folder
Show your best two or three pieces
Offer a concrete next piece of work

say: After positive feedback, ask simply, once: if you know another business owner who could use this, please share my number.

panel.heading: Referrals and the next job
items: Keep proof in one Drive folder
Show your best two or three pieces
Offer a concrete next piece of work

say: And at every handover, suggest a next piece of work with a package name and price, so saying yes is easy.

say: Treat too expensive as a question, not a final no. Find out what they are comparing you to.

Then reduce the scope, not the rate. For 35,000 naira I can do 20 descriptions. Within 18,000 I can do the 10 most important first. You can also split the payment, or let a very low budget go politely.

panel.heading: When a client says too expensive
left: Reduce the scope, not the rate

say: Cutting the price for the same work teaches the client your first price was not real, and pushes you below your minimum rate. If you discount, attach it to something real, like payment in full up front.

panel.heading: When a client says too expensive
left: Reduce the scope, not the rate

say: A monthly package, also called a retainer, is the same service every month. It gives you predictable income with less selling.

card.title: A monthly package pays better
card.note: Total is three months of secured income.

say: For example, Hauwa can give 15 hours a week. In the first 30 days she sends 5 personal pitches a week and aims for 1 to 2 first clients.

panel.heading: Three phases of 30 days
items: Review dates fixed in your calendar

say: In days 31 to 60, she keeps pitching, uses her templates on every job and collects 2 testimonials.

panel.heading: Three phases of 30 days
items: Review dates fixed in your calendar

say: In days 61 to 90, she offers a monthly package, asks for referrals, and raises her price for new clients by 10 percent.

panel.heading: Three phases of 30 days
items: Review dates fixed in your calendar

say: Her review dates are fixed for days 30, 60 and 90. Avoid the common mistakes: targets with no activity, too many channels, and planning more hours than you have.

panel.heading: Three phases of 30 days
items: Review dates fixed in your calendar

say: To remember. Ask specific questions for feedback. Use testimonials only with permission. Reduce the scope, not your rate.
Offer monthly packages. And report your results honestly. Twelve pitches and no clients yet is still a real start.
Now collect your first proof, practise your 30-second explanation, and assemble your Freelance Launch Project with your 90-day plan.
